lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: On 4625 kilohertz, a buzzer has sounded for decades. Sometimes a voice reads words.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: It's a shortwave radio signal. About 25 buzzes a minute, around the clock. It has been on air since about the mid-1970s. The earliest preserved recording is from 1982.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Hobbyists call it "the Buzzer". For years it only buzzed. The first voice message was on December 24, 1997.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: The voice reads a callsign, then a few words and numbers. The callsign has changed several times since.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: On December 11, 2024, it sent 24 messages with 30 different words in one day. A monitoring group called it the most talkative day in the station's history.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Pirates sometimes break in with music or speech. Those events aren't the station itself.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Who runs it? The Russian military is the common assumption. That's never been officially confirmed. A "doomsday signal" theory is widely considered unlikely.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: The signal is real. The purpose is not public.
